investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but have no remaining allocatable capacity (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 121–146 seconds before the eval timed out, the agent VM was never created, and the runner never wrote any required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service outage is present in the supplied packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but have no remaining allocatable capacity (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 121–146 seconds before the eval timed out, the agent VM was never created, and the runner never wrote any required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service outage is present in the supplied packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval received zero evidence — all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. Preemption was also exhausted ("No preemption victims found"). The eval failure is an infrastructure scheduling failure, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).
